image.alt: Golden retriever asleep in a grey corduroy Kendal bolster dog bed on a wooden floor beside a cream sofa

intro_html: Curled tight, chin on the sofa arm, or flat out on the kitchen floor: you already know how they sleep. Our dog beds are sorted by it, with free standard UK delivery on orders over £40.
description_html:
Before you choose between dog beds, watch how yours settles tonight. The tight curl with a nose under the tail. The chin hooked over the sofa arm. The full-length sprawl across the kitchen floor. That habit tells you more about the right bed than any photograph, and most beds here are shaped around one of them.

Start with how they sleep

  • If they curl up tight, choose walls. A dog who tucks in and presses their spine against the nearest edge tends to ignore a flat mat. Nest and donut beds give them sides all the way round.
  • If they lean on things, choose an edge. When their chin is always resting on something, bolster beds and dog sofas put a raised, cushioned edge on one, two, three or four sides.
  • If they sprawl, choose surface. On a walled bed their back legs end up on the floor. A dog mattress lets them step on from any side and stretch the whole length.

Then decide what goes underneath

Fibre filling, used in nests such as Rydal and Wensleydale, is soft and yielding, but it shifts and flattens with use. Foam holds its shape under weight. Memory foam contours to the dog lying on it, and profiled egg-crate foam spreads their weight rather than compressing flat. If they have started to hesitate at the edge of the bed, look at our orthopaedic dog beds, several of which leave the front open or drop it low so there is nothing to climb. A bed is for comfort, not a treatment, so if your dog is in pain please keep talking to your vet.

Size it from the sleeping area

Measure your dog lying on their side, nose to base of tail, and add 15 to 20cm. On walled beds the sides take up part of the listed footprint: the Loweswater XL is 90 × 70cm outside but 72 × 55cm to lie on. Between two sizes, size up. If the bed is going in a crate or a car boot, measure the floor it has to lie on, not the outside of the crate.

Our dog beds: the 100-night trial, and two exceptions

No photo can tell you whether they will actually sleep on it. Your floor can. Most beds here come with a 100-night trial from delivery: if it is not right, we arrange free UK mainland collection and a full refund (one trial per household; damage and other exclusions apply). Two exceptions. Personalised beds, such as Rydal Personalised, are made to order, so they are excluded from the trial and from change-of-mind returns, though your full legal rights apply if one arrives faulty, damaged or not as described. The Whinlatter car seat is a travel accessory, so check its returns eligibility first. Where a memory foam bed also carries a 5-year no-flatten guarantee on its foam core, its product page says so. The trial page has the full terms.

Questions owners ask

Is UK delivery free?

Standard UK delivery is free on orders over £40, and every dog bed here is priced above that. Check the product page for delivery timings and any product-specific lead time before you order; our delivery and returns page covers the rest.

Can I wash the covers?

On most beds the cover comes off, and many wash at 30°C. Follow the sewn-in label, air-dry fully, and never wash or soak the foam. Check coated wipe-clean fabrics against their label before any machine wash, and keep Thirlmere's structured felt out of the machine.

Do you have beds for very large dogs?

Yes. Mardale, Longsleddale and Burnmoor are 132 × 104cm and 20cm deep, and Brotherswater's raised mesh deck is 150 × 95cm.

Still not sure? The Bed Finder asks how they sleep first, then narrows the range to one bed.
claims_to_confirm: Trial applies to 'most' beds: Rydal Personalised is excluded (its own page says so) and the Whinlatter car seat's page says to 'check the returns terms and confirm eligibility'. Confirm the car seat's actual return terms so the copy can state them.

Nine dog beds carry the 'Shopify Collective' tag (e.g. Elterwater, Eskdale, Kentmere, Hawkshead, Seathwaite, Loweswater, Patterdale, Wasdale, Crummock Herringbone). Their pages promise the 100-night trial with free UK mainland collection; confirm PawLunova (not the Collective supplier) can honour that on every one.

Delivery timings: product pages say 'Check delivery timings and any product-specific lead time' but no timing is stated anywhere in the data. The FAQ answer points to product pages; confirm timings are actually shown there (or at checkout).

Guarantee/returns terms link target: product pages say 'Read the full returns and guarantee terms' without a resolvable URL in the snapshot. Copy links to /pages/100-night-trial; confirm that page will carry the guarantee terms too.

Several sizes have no listed dimensions (Rydal High-Sided Nest all sizes, Wensleydale, Tetbury, Haweswater XL, Sawrey Small, Watendlath, Rosthwaite, Braithwaite, Windsor). Sizing advice here is generic; adding measurements would support the size guidance.
All product images in the snapshot have empty alt text; worth adding descriptive alts store-wide.

Store-wide image risk: many product photos carry other brands' leather tabs or labels (seen on Eskdale and Wasdale: 'RALPH & CO', a real UK dog-bed brand; Ennerdale: 'CHAHZ'; Melbreak, Grasmere, Whinlatter, Wastwater, Chatsworth, Mardale, Watendlath and Coniston: other non-PawLunova marks). Selling under PawLunova product names with another brand's mark in the photo risks misleading shoppers about who makes the product (CPRs/DMCC, ASA CAP). Confirm supplier and image rights, or replace, before launch.
